title: How Much Does It Cost to Remodel a House? [2026 Data]
summary: Get a breakdown of home remodeling costs by project, from a minor bathroom update to a full kitchen remodel. Learn what factors affect the cost of a home remodel.

Cost Insights:


-


Whole house remodels cost **$52,000** on average, but your project can range from **$3,000** to **$225,000** depending on scope and room selection.


-


The room type and materials you choose drive your costs, with kitchens and bathrooms needing more investment than living rooms or bedrooms.


-


You should budget for building permits and potential remediation work like mold removal or structural repairs when planning your remodel.


-


[Hiring a local home remodeling professional](https://www.angi.com/nearme/home-remodeling/) ensures your project is done well and boosts the overall home value.


In 2026, the national average cost to remodel a house is **$52,000** . Most homeowners spend between **$19,000** and **$88,000** , with the cost driven by project scope, room selection, and material choices. For a personalized estimate, a local remodeling professional can help you plan your budget.


## Home Remodeling Costs by Project Scope: Room Type Breakdown


[Home renovations](https://www.angi.com/articles/complete-house-renovation-cost.htm) focus on cosmetic upgrades, while remodels involve rebuilding or changing a room's purpose, with average costs ranging from **$10,500 to $12,000** . Remodeling one room costs less than tackling the entire home.


Room size is also a key cost driver, with larger spaces requiring a bigger budget. Costs vary significantly depending on which room you choose to remodel, as shown in the breakdown below:


Room Type Average Cost in 2026 Average Cost Range in 2026


Bathroom $12,000 $6,600–$18,000


Kitchen $27,000 $15,00–$42,000


Basement $22,000 $12,000–$35,000


Garage $18,000 $7,000–$30,000


Living room $8,000 $2,500–$15,000


Bedroom $20,000 $12,000–$28,000


Dining room $20,000 $7,000–$25,000


Laundry room $11,000 $6,000–$17,000


Attic $20,000 $7,500–$35,000


Exterior $10,500 $5,000–$30,000


### Bathroom Remodeling Costs


[Bathroom remodel costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-bathroom-remodel-cost.htm) typically range from **$2,500 to $30,000** , depending on what you plan to update, whether that's flooring, fixtures, paint, or countertops. Projects that relocate plumbing or electrical systems can push costs to **$80,000** or more. Choosing luxury materials such as custom cabinetry, radiant floor heating, or a grand walk-in shower will also move your budget toward the higher end of the range.


### Kitchen Remodeling Costs


The[cost of a kitchen remodel](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-should-kitchen-remodel-cost.htm) averages **$26,974** , though the range is wide depending on project scope. A minor remodel runs **$10,000 to $20,000** and typically requires prioritizing one or two upgrades, such as refacing cabinetry, upgrading countertops, or replacing appliances.


A complete kitchen overhaul, which may involve changing the layout, removing walls, adding an island, and installing high-end materials, can reach **$65,000 to $130,000** or more.


### Basement Remodeling Costs


[Basement remodels cost](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-basement-remodeling-cost.htm) an average of **$22,800** , with a typical range of **$3,250 to $56,000** depending on size, materials, and intended use. Most basement projects require coordinating multiple professionals, including a general contractor, plumber, and electrician.


### Garage Remodeling Costs


Garage conversions are among the most versatile remodeling projects, with homeowners spending **$7,000 to $30,000** and an average cost of **$18,000** . The biggest factors affecting[garage remodel costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-remodel-garage.htm) are square footage, the type of conversion, and whether you need to add utilities such as plumbing, electrical, or HVAC.


### Living Room Remodeling Costs


The average[living room remodel cost](https://www.angi.com/articles/living-room-remodel-cost.htm) is **$8,000** , though a simple cosmetic refresh can cost as little as **$500** . A large-scale remodel that includes added storage, updated electrical, new floors, fresh paint, and window treatments can push costs upward of **$40,000** .


### Bedroom Remodeling Costs


[Bedroom remodel costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/bedroom-remodel-cost.htm) range from **$12,000 to $28,000** , with an average of **$20,000** , and the final price rises with larger room sizes, luxury materials, or add-ons like a built-in wardrobe.

### Dining Room Remodeling Costs


The average[cost of a dining room remodel](https://www.angi.com/articles/dining-room-remodel-cost.htm) is **$20,000** , with a simple cosmetic project coming in at **$7,000** or less and a full gut-to-studs remodel running **$25,000** or more.


### Laundry Room Remodeling Costs


[Laundry room remodel costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/laundry-room-remodel-cost.htm) average around **$11,000** , with basic updates like fresh paint and new appliances starting as low as **$1,800** . Changing the layout, choosing high-end appliances, or adding custom finishes can push the total to **$40,000** or more.


### Attic Remodeling Costs


[Attic finishing costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/cost-to-finish-attic.htm) average **$20,000** , with most projects falling between **$7,500 and $35,000** depending on scope. Adding storage is the more affordable path, while converting the attic into livable space drives costs higher, particularly when electrical work, plumbing, and HVAC are involved.


### Exterior Remodeling Costs


Homeowners spend an average of **$10,500** on[exterior remodeling costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/home-exterior-remodel-cost.htm) , with common projects including siding replacement, new windows, roof replacement, landscaping, and exterior painting.


## Home Remodeling Cost Factors: What Determines the Price?


While the type of project has the biggest influence on home remodeling costs, factors like accessibility, materials, location, and demolition also shape your final budget.


### Demolition and Prep


Are you planning to tear out old walls, flooring, cabinetry, or fixtures? Demolition is labor-intensive, and it requires skilled professionals to do it safely and efficiently. The extent of the prep work will influence your project's final budget.


### Permits


For a major home remodel,[building permit costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-building-permit-cost.htm) typically run **$500 to $2,500** , with fees varying by location and project scope. Your contractor will manage the permitting process, and that cost will be folded into their final quote.


### Materials


Home remodeling materials cost anywhere from **$15 to $150 per square foot** , with luxury choices pushing you toward the upper end. For example, a porcelain tile shower runs **$2 to $30 per square foot** , while a cultured marble shower can cost **$40 to $65 per square foot** .


### Accessibility


Hard-to-reach areas such as tall ceilings or narrow stairwells can increase labor costs, since navigating ladders, scaffolding, or confined spaces makes tasks more time-consuming and introduces additional safety considerations.

### Location


Where you live directly affects what you pay for a remodel, since labor rates, material costs, and living expenses vary by region. Homeowners in major metropolitan areas generally pay more than those in rural locations.


### Repairs and Remediations


Unexpected costs are common during remodels, particularly in older homes where electrical and plumbing systems may need replacement, adding thousands to your budget. Hidden issues like water damage, rot, mold, asbestos, lead paint, or structural problems can surface once work begins, so it pays to budget for remediation from the start. Costs for these repairs vary by problem type, as shown in the breakdown below.


-


[Water damage restoration](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-repair-water-damage.htm) : **$1,400–$6,400**


-


[Mold remediation](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-mold-remediation-service-cost.htm) : **$1,200–$3,800**


-


[Asbestos removal](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-asbestos-removal-cost.htm) : **$1,200–$3,200**


-


[Lead paint removal](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-cost-removing-lead-paint.htm) : **$1,500–$5,500**


-


[Structural problems](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-foundation-repair-cost.htm) : **$2,200–$8,100**


-


[Upgrading electrical panel](https://www.angi.com/articles/ask-angie-what-does-it-cost-upgrade-200-amps.htm) : **$1,200–$2,000**


-


[Replacing old plumbing](https://www.angi.com/articles/cost-to-repipe-a-house.htm) : **$1,500–$15,000**


### Post-Construction Cleanup


Most contractors include basic cleanup in their initial quote, but if you want a thorough clean once the work is done, hiring a[professional post-construction cleaning service](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-clean-construction-site.htm) typically costs between **$275 and $710** .


## Home Remodel Pro Costs: What Homeowners Pay


Labor accounts for about 40% to 60% of your total home remodel budget, making it one of the largest line items to plan for. A[home remodeling professional near you](https://www.angi.com/nearme/home-remodeling/) can provide an accurate quote based on your specific project.


### General Contractor


[General contractors charge](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-do-general-contractors-charge-hourly-rates.htm) **$50 to $150 per hour** , though most large remodels are priced on a per-project basis rather than hourly. A general contractor oversees every phase of a home remodeling project, from planning and permits to demo, design, and inspections, and coordinates the right subcontractors for specialized work.


### Electrician


The[cost of an electrician](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-hire-electrician.htm) runs **$50 to $130 per hour** , depending on their expertise and your location. Any remodel involving electrical work, such as[rewiring a house](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-rewire-house.htm) , installing new outlets, adding a ceiling fan, or upgrading your electric panel, requires a licensed electrician.


### Plumber


[Plumber costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/plumber-cost.htm) run **$50 to $150 per hour** for this type of work. Kitchen and bathroom remodels often require a plumber to handle tasks like replacing faucets and fixtures, rerouting plumbing, installing new toilets, fixing leaky pipes, or adding a shower.


### Additional Contractors


Depending on the scope of your remodel, you may need to bring in additional specialists beyond a general contractor, electrician, or plumber, and costs vary by trade and project complexity:


-


[HVAC technician](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-hire-hvac-expert.htm) : **$100–$250 per hour**


-


[Flooring specialist](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-should-my-new-floor-cost.htm) : **$1,530–$4,850**


-


[Drywall installer](https://www.angi.com/articles/what-cost-install-drywall.htm) : **$990–$3,210**


-


[Window installer](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-window-replacement-cost.htm) : **$300–$2,500** **per window**


-


[Professional painter](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-paint-room.htm) : **$400–$1,600** **per room**


-


[Structural engineer](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-structural-engineer-cost.htm) : **$345–$775**


-


[Interior designer](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-hire-interior-designer.htm) : **$2,055–$15,210**


## Home Remodel vs. Renovation

When planning your project, you’ve probably heard the terms["renovation" and "remodel,"](https://www.angi.com/articles/renovate-vs-remodel.htm) but they actually mean different things. A home renovation focuses on updating the existing room without fundamentally changing its layout or purpose. Renovations include cosmetic updates like new flooring, countertops, light fixtures, or paint colors.


On the other hand, remodeling involves altering the structure and design of a room. The changes are usually more extensive, such as changing the layout, removing walls, relocating plumbing, adding features like a kitchen island, and converting unfinished rooms into living space.


Here’s a breakdown of the differences between home renovations and remodels:


Renovation Remodel


Costs less Costs more


Aims to restore or refresh a room Aims to rebuild or change the purpose of a room


Involves cosmetic improvements and minor updates Involves structural, functional, or layout changes


Examples include updated painting, flooring, and fixtures Examples include moved walls, home additions, and rerouted plumbing or electrical


Permit not always required Permit is often required


DIY-friendly in many cases Likely requires a professional


## DIY Remodeling vs. Hiring a Pro


Labor makes up **40% to 60%** of your home remodel cost. The average homeowner could save thousands by taking on a DIY job, and they’ll only pay for materials.


That said, doing a home remodel yourself isn’t advisable. These major projects often require working with structural, electrical, and plumbing systems. Making mistakes can set you back thousands of dollars—and they can also be downright dangerous, both for yourself and your home.


Professionals produce quality work in a shorter time period. They also have the necessary skills and experience to complete the job without complications. If you’re looking to remodel your home, reach out to a[home remodeling professional near you](https://www.angi.com/nearme/home-remodeling/) for a quote.

## How to Save Money While Remodeling Your Home


Remodels are a major expense, but you can still save money on your project. Here are some cost-cutting tips:


-


Consider DIYing certain aspects of the project, such as painting,[installing a backsplash](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-kitchen-backsplash-cost.htm) , tearing out old carpeting, or swapping light fixtures.


-


Opt for mid-range materials instead of luxury ones. Stay away from the least expensive options, as you may notice lower quality.


-


Limit the amount of customizations in your remodel.


-


Get quotes from at least three contractors to find the best rate.


-


Consider[refinishing cabinets](https://www.angi.com/articles/when-refinish-kitchen-cabinets-instead-refacing.htm) or flooring instead of replacing them.


-


Handle the post-construction cleanup yourself.


## Does Remodeling Increase Home Value?


Home remodeling projects often increase home value—sometimes by **60%** to more than **100%** —but the exact return on investment (ROI) depends on the project. The key is choosing remodels with a broad appeal that align with the value of the home and its surrounding neighborhood.


Here’s the average ROI for several different home remodeling projects:
